subject: orthopaedics
title: Perthes and SCFE: contain the young, pin the slip

steps.tx: **Perthes disease** affects boys aged four to eight years who limp because the femoral head loses its blood supply. The **Waldenstrom** stages run from initial change through fragmentation and reossification to the healed phase. A **crescent sign** shows a subchondral fracture, and the Herring system grades the lateral pillar height. Younger children under six remodel well, while older children more often need containment surgery.
steps.say: A young boy develops a painless or mildly painful limp over several weeks. Blood supply to the ball of the hip joint fails and the bone softens. Films show the head becoming dense, fragmented and later slowly rebuilding itself. A thin fracture line under the joint surface carries prognostic importance for outcome. Very young children reshape the head well as they continue growing.

steps.tx: This pelvic film shows a **sclerotic fragmented** right femoral head with a **crescent sign** and a labelled Herring lateral pillar. The left hip looks normal, which makes the contrast easy to read at a glance. The image matters because Perthes staging and pillar height guide containment decisions in children. For the exam, match this dense fragmented head with a limping boy aged four to eight years.
steps.say: One hip shows a dense and broken ball while the other hip looks completely normal. A thin pale line under the joint surface marks the small fracture described in the labels. The outer column of the head helps doctors grade severity and predict the outcome. Comparing both sides makes the abnormal head stand out clearly for learners. This appearance in a young limping boy should bring the diagnosis to mind.

vis.caption: Pelvic radiograph showing Perthes disease right hip. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In this frog lateral film a **slipped capital femoral epiphysis** displaces posteriorly and inferiorly in an obese adolescent. Hip pain may present as knee pain, so the **Klein line** along the femoral neck misses the head in a slip. The **Southwick** angle grades severity, and endocrine disease needs exclusion in atypical cases. An unstable slip that cannot bear weight needs urgent referral and protection.
steps.say: The film shows the growth plate slipping at the top of the thigh bone. The ball moves backward and downward compared with its normal position. Adolescents with high body weight will face the greatest risk of this injury. Pain may appear in the knee even though the hip causes the problem. A child who cannot bear any weight needs urgent specialist care.

vis.alt: Frog-lateral hip X-ray showing posterior-inferior displacement of the femoral epiphysis in SCFE.
vis.caption: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) on frog-lateral X-ray. Image: Dr.Vijaya chandar, CC0/PD, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Fixation uses a single cannulated screw placed **in situ** across the physis, without forceful reduction of the slip. A stable slip follows a planned schedule, while an **unstable slip** needs urgent gentle positioning and fixation. Forceful reduction can kill the blood supply and cause **avascular necrosis** of the head. The guide wire should pass centre to centre, and image views confirm the final position.
steps.say: One screw across the growth plate holds the slip firmly in its current position. Surgeons avoid forcing the ball back because that manoeuvre can destroy its blood supply. A slip that still allows weight bearing follows a planned operating schedule. A slip that prevents weight bearing needs urgent and very gentle handling. Careful wire placement under imaging control prevents penetration into the joint.

steps.tx: A transient synovitis settles with pain free intervals, while a septic hip needs urgent aspiration and washout by **Kocher** guided judgement. Night pain with weight loss raises concern for **lymphoma** rather than a simple hip problem. The **Stulberg** grade describes the final head shape and predicts adult arthritis risk. Counselling on sport limits and lifelong review completes care for the deformed hip.
steps.say: Several disorders imitate hip disease in a limping child and need separation. Temporary joint irritation settles and leaves pain free gaps between episodes. Joint infection instead progresses quickly and demands urgent drainage and washing. Night pain with weight loss should raise suspicion of a blood malignancy. The final shape of the healed head predicts arthritis in adult life.
